prior_negative_finding.evidence: WHAT I CHECKED. (1) I read the 1862's own end of the Good Friday liturgy, text-layer lines 33352-33460, printed pp. 178-179. After the priest's communion it prints `Quod ore sumpsimus, Domine...` and then, in terms, `Non dicitur Corpus tuum, Domine, nec Postcommunio, nec Placeat tibi, nec datur benedictio: sed, facta reverentia Altari, Sacerdos cum ministris discedit`. The pre-1955 rite has NO prayers after Communion on this day; the 1955 Ordo added three, because it restored the Communion of the people. (2) I then searched the whole 1862 by incipit and by four distinctive phrases -- `Super p.pulum tuum`, `benedicti. copi.sa`, `indulg.ntia veniat`, `succr.scat`, `devota mente` -- over the flattened, dehyphenated stream. `Super populum` occurs many times as the Lenten rubric `Oratio super populum` and once as `benedictio copiosa descendat: quae et sanctificationem nobis clementer...`, which is a DIFFERENT Lenten super populum prayer, not this one. `devota mente` and `succrescat` occur nowhere in the book. SAME CANDOUR AS FOR no. 924: the prayer is very likely ancient, but no tracked public-domain witness carries it, so it may not be published from this facsimile on the evidence available here. || THREE-BOOK SWEEP ADDED IN THE SECOND PASS. The lane's first pass swept the 1862 alone. On the coordinator's rule that new-matter needs the whole shelf behind it, I re-swept all three tracked public-domain witnesses -- 1862 Pustet (108,905 lines), 1604 Vatican typica (63,205 lines), 1570 Venice (84,443 lines), the last two with long s folded to s -- on rare word PAIRS taken adjacent in the 1962 text and matched fuzzily (>=0.85 character similarity, same initial letter) within a twelve-word window, so neither a lost ornamental capital nor a damaged accent can hide a hit. POSITIVE CONTROL for the procedure: it fires on prayers this lane proved present (oblationibus+hostiarum 3 hits in the 1862, hostiarum+initiata 2, productum+silice 1, paschalia+inflammari 1, illustras+conserva 1, segetum+spinarum 1). RESULT: zero in all three books on succrescat+firmetur, firmetur+eundem, devota+recoluit, recoluit+copiosa, copiosa+indulgentia, tribuatur+succrescat, succrescat+redemptio, redemptio+firmetur. Single token succrescat occurs nowhere in any of the three. The two isolated ones (indulgentia+consolatio in the 1862, recoluit+descendat in the 1862 and 1570) are common-word coincidences, opened and not this prayer.

whole_expression_merits.whole_expression_argument: Consider the resulting prayer as one adapted blessing: the entire inherited ordered fivefold petition remains consecutive and unchanged, addressed to the same people with the same descent-of-blessing construction. The inserted nine-word relative clause identifies those people by the liturgical action just completed: devout remembrance of the Son's Passion and death. It adds no new requested gift, image, comparison or independent petition. The reordered supplication and the received same-Christ conclusion/response are conventional liturgical framing. On that bounded view, the whole can be proposed as a functional contextual adaptation of the single old blessing, rather than a newly selected collection of old fragments. This is an arguable finite qualified-nonoriginal-adaptation assessment at moderate confidence, not proof of an exact ancient whole or an adopted publication conclusion. The full relative clause and the new placement must still be judged as part of the resulting whole.
whole_expression_merits.strongest_contrary: The newly inserted full relative clause gives a specific commemorative rationale and ties the old blessing to the Good Friday assembly. Even where its vocabulary is conventional, this substantive clause and the resulting whole-prayer arrangement cannot be classed as mere spelling, inflection or punctuation. No exact premodern witness for that entire target clause in this whole has been established. The antiquity of the five petitions and the conventional conclusion do not alone settle originality of the modern whole.

whole_expression_merits.whole_expression_argument: Consider the resulting prayer as one adapted collect: its complete inherited movement remains divine restoration through Christ's Passion, a request to preserve mercy's work within the speakers, and the purpose of living in perpetual devotion in relation to the mystery. The modern wording makes death explicit, casts restoration as accomplished, names the mercy already central to the old petition, uses a collective singular work, and connects the petition to participation after Communion. The changes adjust the old collect to its specific liturgical use without adding a new requested benefit, metaphor, narrative or separate source-selected petition. With the independently witnessed conventional same-Christ conclusion and response, that whole is a viable finite qualified-nonoriginal-adaptation proposal at moderate confidence. This is an inference about the measured adaptation, not a grant based on familiar words or the old prayer's age. The cumulative changes in address, tense, number and celebration/participation still require a whole-expression decision.
whole_expression_merits.strongest_contrary: The accumulated changes recast the divine address, explicitly add death, shift the restoration from present to completed action, change plural works to one work, and replace celebration with participation in the mystery. These coordinated theological and rhetorical choices must be considered together. Conventional vocabulary and a recognizable old prayer skeleton do not prove that the whole modern arrangement is unprotected. No exact premodern whole target witness has been established.

case.Latin: Hostias tibi, Domine, in odorem suavitatis offerimus: et praesta; ut, beati Roberti monitis et exemplis edocti, per semitam mandatorum tuorum dilatato corde curramus. Per Dominum nostrum.
case.English: We offer you sacrificial offerings, O Lord, as a sweet fragrance; and grant that, instructed by the counsels and examples of blessed Robert, we may run with an enlarged heart along the path of your commandments. Through our Lord.
case.public_notice: Qualified United States editorial assessment of this exact adaptation under publication policy section 1 priority 6; moderate confidence. The source record preserves the opposing originality argument. This is not holder permission or an unqualified public-domain claim. Triptych owns only its editorial carrier.

complete_merits.positive_whole_expression_argument: Taken as a whole, the prayer is a compact conventional offertory: offer sacrificial gifts as a sweet odor, then ask to follow the commandments with an enlarged heart through the saint’s teaching and examples. The 1923 prayer already links these offerings, their sweet odor and Robert’s examples. The older Berchmans Postcommunion contains the complete concluding commandment-path/enlarged-heart petition with viam; the older Alphonsus Collect contains the instruction/example idiom. The target’s syntax joins these conventional functions in their expected offertory sequence. This gives a concrete, finite argument that the remaining changes do not introduce sufficient new expressive authorship in this particular complete prayer.
complete_merits.strongest_contrary: The 1923 whole prayer asks that offerings be accepted and that the worshippers immolate a holocaust of fidelity; the 1931 prayer instead states the offering and asks to run the commandments. Neither older source supplies the whole target. Hostias tibi ... offerimus, et praesta; ut, the combined monitis et exemplis edocti, and per semitam replace old syntax and select a different movement of thought. A new arrangement of unprotected material may itself be protected. The 1931 title and 23 December approval defeat the catalogue-1929 shortcut.
complete_merits.recommended_disposition: Submit as the stronger Bellarmine candidate for a narrowly reasoned ambiguous-but-defensible merits decision. This is an argument for Root to evaluate, not an established public-domain finding. Hold persists unless that exact complete expression and both publication languages/surfaces are admitted.
complete_merits.what_would_change: Independent review accepts the complete-expression argument and Root explicitly adopts this exact body, or a new earlier whole witness or exact permission supersedes the merits route.
complete_merits.previous_negative_findings: The1923 whole prayer is materially different. The1931 source replaces both the offering syntax and the second petition, combines older motifs in a new arrangement, and has explicit23Dec1931 approval. No complete pre1931 target witness is established.

complete_merits.not_new_evidence: No additional historical prayer witness was acquired in this four-case drafting step; fresh study English and current official copyright sources do not supply an old target witness.

case.Latin: Sumptis, Domine, salutaribus sacramentis: da, quaesumus; ut, meritis et intercessione beatae Virginis Mariae in caelum assumptae, ad resurrectionis gloriam perducamur. Per Dominum.
case.English: Having received the saving sacraments, O Lord, we ask you to grant that, through the merits and intercession of the Blessed Virgin Mary assumed into heaven, we may be led to the glory of the resurrection. Through our Lord.
case.public_notice: Qualified United States editorial assessment of this exact adaptation under publication policy section 1 priority 6; moderate confidence. The source record preserves the opposing originality argument. This is not holder permission or an unqualified public-domain claim. Triptych owns only its editorial carrier.

complete_merits.positive_whole_expression_argument: The complete target follows a conventional Postcommunion sequence: after receiving saving sacraments, ask through the saint’s merits/intercession to be brought to resurrection glory. Wilson 1915 prints the exact opening in a complete older Postcommunion; Mame 1922 prints the exact final resurrection-glory clause in the Holy Shroud Collect; the 1923 Bellarmine Collect prints the merits/intercession formula. The intermediate naming of the Blessed Virgin and her Assumption is an ordinary identification of the feast, and the connective da, quaesumus; ut is formulaic. Considered as this short complete prayer, rather than as a percentage of old words, the proposed argument is that the residual authorship is a conventional functional joining of inherited prayer clauses, without a distinctive new expressive passage.
complete_merits.strongest_contrary: No old witness here prints the whole Assumption target. The 1950 Mass deliberately joins reception of sacraments, Mary’s heavenly Assumption and the worshippers’ future resurrection. That particular theological progression can be expressive selection/arrangement even if every ingredient is traditional. The connector and full Marian application are not established as an exact older combined unit. Lasance’s Signum magnum Mass occurs on an ordinary numbered page in a mixed facsimile and cannot be dated 1945 from pagination. A prior agent’s ready label never became Root admission, and its vanished bodies are not evidence.
complete_merits.recommended_disposition: Submit separately for a finite ambiguous-but-defensible merits decision, with the complete 1950 arrangement squarely before Root. It has a plausible conventional-formula argument but no established older whole witness. Continue hold unless the exact body and the new study English route are expressly admitted.
complete_merits.what_would_change: Independent full-source review and a fresh Root decision on this precise whole-expression argument; alternatively a new dated complete earlier witness or exact permission.
complete_merits.previous_negative_findings: No whole pre1950 Assumption target witness has been established. The1950 arrangement combines received sacraments, merits/intercession of Mary assumed into heaven, and resurrection glory. Lasance has the1950 Mass on unlettered pages; ordinary pagination does not make its English part of1945. Prior ready report never reached Root adoption and its old bodies are absent.
complete_merits.new_evidence_since_stop: Actual complete acquired Acta III and VI page images and the true 1931 fascicle/approval chronology; complete old formula witnesses and target image collation. For Assumption specifically, Wilson 1915 exact opening and Mame 1922 exact ending. These are new source findings relative to the old stop, not newly discovered in this final drafting step. A further bounded official acquisition in this drafting step supplies AAS 42 (1950), pp. 793–795: new Mass and decree dated 31 October 1950, issue footer 4 November 1950. It is an archival OCR reconstruction, not a native facsimile.
complete_merits.not_new_evidence: No new pre-1931 complete target witness. The official 1950 digital rendering has visible OCR errors, including perducantur at the Postcommunion, and is not used as an exact prayer-body authority. New study English and current copyright sources do not supply an old target witness.
